info.title: Vaquill India API
info.description:
Public API for Indian primary law: Central and State Acts, the instruments of the principal regulators, and their individual sections.

**Authentication**: Pass your API key as `Authorization: Bearer vq_key_...` (preferred) or in the `X-API-Key` header. The `api_key` query parameter also works where a header cannot be set, but a URL ends up in logs and browser history. Sending two different keys in one request is rejected with a 401. The same key works against the US API; the two share one credit balance.

**Credits**: Each call costs API credits. See `GET /api/v1/api-credits/pricing` for the full pricing matrix.

## Coverage

Central, State and Union Territory enactments, addressable down to the individual section, plus the instruments of the principal regulators. Regulators covered include SEBI, RBI, MCA, IRDAI, TRAI, DGFT, MOEFCC and CPCB.

`GET /acts/filters` is free and returns the live section count behind every `category`, `state` and `department` value, so read volumes from there rather than from this page.

`sourceUrl` points at the publisher's own document where we hold a live one, and is `null` otherwise. India Code migrated hosts in August 2026 and re-minted its identifiers, so links into the old site no longer resolve; we return nothing rather than a link that 404s. `pdfUrl` and `textUrl` are served from our own mirror and are unaffected.

## Scope

This document describes the **India** surface only. US statutes are a separate document at `/external/openapi.json`, so an MCP client configured here sees Indian tools and nothing else.

get.summary: Get your India API credit balance
get.description:
Returns the credits this API key's account can spend right now.

**Free.** Never charged, so it is safe to poll for low-balance alerting or to
pre-flight a batch job.

**Authentication:** any valid `vq_key_` key. No particular scope is required.

Credits are account-wide and are **not** split by jurisdiction: the same balance
funds the India legislation endpoints and the United States primary-law
endpoints, from one ledger. This route and the United States
`GET /api/v1/credits/balance` therefore report the same number, and spending on
either surface moves both.

Read `bySource` before assuming a balance is durable: `subscription` credits are
use-it-or-lose-it at the period end, while `payg` credits you purchased persist
and burn last. `nextExpiry` tells you what is about to be forfeited and when.

## Example

```bash
curl https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/in/credits/balance \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"
```

200.description: Current spendable balance for the calling key's account.

401.description: Missing, malformed or unrecognised API key. Note this endpoint accepts ONLY a `vq_key_` API key; a dashboard session token is rejected here.

429.description: Request-rate ceiling exceeded. Retry after the `Retry-After` header. Being throttled says nothing about your balance.

Browse Indian acts, regulations and legislation with filters.

Use this endpoint to **discover act IDs** for the other routes here.

It enumerates **every served act** and pages over a total order, so walking the
offsets returns each act exactly once with a `total` that does not move
underneath you. Read that `total` for how many there are.

The listing is a dated **snapshot**, rebuilt on the ingest cadence. An act
ingested after that build is served by `POST /acts/search` and the act routes

get.summary: Map a repealed code to its replacement
get.description:
Section-by-section mapping from a repealed Indian criminal code to the 2023
code that replaced it, in force from 1 July 2024.

Pass either side of the pair: `ipc` and `bns` both return the IPC to BNS
mapping, `crpc` and `bnss` both return CrPC to BNSS.

**Coverage**: `ipc`/`bns` and `crpc`/`bnss`. `iea`/`bsa` are accepted but
return 404 until the Evidence Act mapping lands, rather than an empty list
that would read as "nothing changed".

of Police Research and Development, an attached office of India's Ministry of
Home Affairs. The `coverage.source` block on every response names the exact
document and links to it.

**Both codes are live law at once.** The repealed code still governs offences
committed before 1 July 2024, for the lifetime of pending trials, so this is a

get.description:
Describe the corpus behind this API: how many acts and provisions it holds, how
they break down by jurisdiction, regulator and status, and how DEEP that holding
goes.

**Cost: free.**

Read the `depth` block before building on this API. It answers four independent
questions, because "we hold the act" and "we hold what amended it" are different
claims and only one of them is true for most of the corpus:

- `actsWithText` is every act we serve;
- `actsWithAmendmentEvents` is the much smaller set for which we hold parsed
  amendment records;
- `actsClaimingAmendmentsWithoutEvents` is the known gap between them, published
  so that an empty amendment list is legible as a gap rather than as a claim
  that nothing ever changed.

Two different kinds of count appear here and they are labelled. `passages` in
the breakdown lists is faceted live and exact right now. The act-level numbers
in `totals` and `depth` come from a full distinct-act scan, and `measuredOn`
says when it ran. Do not divide one into the other.

categoryLegend.meaning: Legislation of the Union Parliament, and central subordinate instruments made under it.
Legislation of a State or Union Territory legislature, and state subordinate instruments. The `state` filter narrows within this.

caveats.actCountsAreDated: Act-level counts come from a full distinct-act scan run on 2026-09-06. Passage counts in this response are live. The two are measured differently on purpose and should not be divided into each other.
caveats.sectionsAreDistinctActSectionPairs: `sections` counts distinct (act, section) pairs. It is NOT the passage count: a section spans about 3.4 passages, so dividing passages by sections is the only safe direction and multiplying is not.
caveats.amendmentCoverage: Structured amendment events are held for 1061 acts. A further 840 acts carry a non-zero amendment count with no parseable footnote behind it; those return an empty event list and say so in their coverage block. Of 32808 records held, 17333 carry an effective …
caveats.textCurrency: We serve the publisher's text as published. We do NOT apply amendments to it. Every amendment event carries an appliedStatus saying so, so currency never has to be inferred from silence.
caveats.repealStatusIsAClaim: act_status and repealedBy are the publisher's claims. We do not verify that a repealing Act was brought into force, and at least one repeal on record involves an Act that never commenced.
caveats.retiredActsAreNotDeleted: 703 acts are retired from the served corpus, either withdrawn by the publisher or duplicates of an act we kept. Nothing was deleted.

get.summary: Resolve a citation to a provision
get.description:
Turn a citation a lawyer would type into the provision it names.

**Cost: 2 credits.** A malformed citation is a 422 and is NOT charged. Every
other outcome is, including `not_found`: a confident negative is the answer.

Accepts what Indian practice actually writes, not what a style guide prescribes.
Three published standards exist and they disagree about element order, while the
most common real form, `u/s 302 IPC`, appears in none of them. So order does not
matter, and all of these work:

    u/s 302 IPC
    Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
    s.302 IPC
    S. 376(2)(g), IPC
    clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 302 IPC
    O. 39 R. 1 CPC
    Art. 21 of the Constitution
    Regulation 24 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
    Maharashtra Act No. LXXVII of 2018

🔴 **Read `status` before reading `candidates`.** `ambiguous` is a real answer
and it is charged, because narrowing a citation to two named enactments is the
work. The commonest cause is the 2023 recodification: after 1 July 2024,
`s. 302` names both IPC 302 (murder) and BNS 302 (uttering words to wound
religious feelings), while BNS 103 is murder. Both codes are live law
simultaneously for the lifetime of pending trials, so this endpoint will not
choose for you. Send `asAtDate` and it will.

`r/w` ("read with") is split into separate citations and each is resolved.

get.summary: Every recorded amendment to one provision
get.description:
The amendment record for a single provision: what changed, which Act changed it,
which of that Act's sections did so, when it took effect where the publisher
records a date, and the wording it replaced where the publisher quotes it.

**Cost: 2 credits.** An empty history for a provision we hold IS the answer and
is charged; the `coverage` block tells you whether it is empty because nothing
changed or because we hold no parsed record.

**Read `appliedStatus` on every event.** It is `not_applied` throughout, because
the text this API serves is the publisher's published text and we do not edit
it. That is a deliberate, stated position rather than an omission: you should
never have to infer currency from silence.

**`asOf` returns a TIMELINE, not text.** We hold amendment events and no
versioned text, so there is no honest way to render this provision as it stood
on a date. Passing `asOf` tells you how many recorded amendments had taken
effect by then, how many had not, and how many carry no date at all. `isBounded`
true means we hold no recorded event affecting that date, which is not the same
as there having been none.

Coverage is real and uneven: many acts carry a non-zero amendment count with no
parseable footnote behind it, and about half the records we do hold carry no
effective date. Read the `coverage` block on this response for the provision you
asked about, and the free `GET /acts/coverage` for the corpus-wide split
(`depth.actsWithAmendmentEvents` against
`depth.actsClaimingAmendmentsWithoutEvents`).

get.summary: Is this act still law, and who says so
get.description:
Everything we know about an act's standing, kept in three separate vocabularies
that are deliberately never collapsed into one verdict.

**Cost: 1 credit.**

- `publisherStatus` is `act_status` exactly as India Code records it. Their
  word.
- `servedStatus` is ours: whether this API answers for the act, or has retired
  it as withdrawn by the publisher or as a duplicate of one we kept.
- `repealClaim` is the publisher's repeal record WITH its source, and with the
  caveat that we do not verify whether the repealing instrument was itself
  brought into force.

That last distinction is not pedantry. India Code lists the Industrial Disputes
Act, 1947 as repealed by Act 37 of 2020, the Industrial Relations Code, which
has never been commenced. Serving that as flatly "repealed" would be wrong, so
this endpoint does not.

A retired act answers here with `servedStatus: retired` and the reason, rather
than 404ing, because "we deliberately withdrew this" is a more useful answer
than "no such thing".

enactmentDateRaw.description: The publisher's own string, when it differs from `enactmentDate`.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: How to cite the act, as the publisher titles it. Present only on index-backed listings.

sectionCount.title: Sectioncount
sectionCount.description: Sections we hold for this act, so a caller can size a fetch before making it. Present only on index-backed listings.

ActListItem.title: ActListItem
ActListItem.description: Lightweight act summary for browsing and discovery.

note.title: Note
note.description: Always set on this endpoint, naming the source that answered. On the normal path it carries the act index's BUILD DATE, because the listing is a snapshot and an act ingested after that date reaches search before it reaches here. If the index is unavailable the note is prefixed `DEGRADED:` and states the shortfall. A gap a caller can see is not the same as one they cannot.

processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems
processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.

creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed
creditsConsumed.description: Credits ACTUALLY charged for this call. Read this rather than assuming the list price: refunded work bills 0.

ActMeta.title: ActMeta
ActMeta.description:
What this call cost and how long it took.

🔴 Added 2026-09-06. Five of the six original routes returned NO statement
of what they billed: `/text` (3 credits), `/amendments` (5), `/list` (1),
`/filters` (0) and `/corresponding-provisions` (1). The house rule on the
US surface is that `creditsConsumed` is the CONTRACT and the list price is
not, and it matters most exactly where refunds happen -- `/text` refunds on
a missing act, `/corresponding-provisions` refunds when a mapping does not
exist yet. Without this field a caller cannot tell a refunded call from a
charged one, and has to reconcile against the ledger to find out.

sections.title: Sections
sections.description: Sections of this act it cross-refers to.

totalActs.title: Totalacts
totalActs.description: Distinct enactments this provision names, before the cap on rows. `acts` is shorter than this when the provision names more than the cap; `truncated` says so.

totalSections.title: Totalsections
totalSections.description: Distinct own-act sections cross-referred, before the cap on rows.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: True when either list was cut to the row cap. This route is not paged: one provision's own outbound edges are a short list, and the cap exists only so a malformed passage cannot return unbounded output.

resolvedFrom.description: How your act_id or section number was matched, when it did not match exactly as sent. Null when it did.

total.title: Total
total.description: Passages in the corpus matching the filters. This is the size of the haystack, not the number of results you can page through: a single section spans several passages, and relevance gating plus act+section dedup run after retrieval. Treat it as an upper bound and a signal to narrow your filters, not as a result count.

totalPages.title: Totalpages
totalPages.description: Pages actually reachable, derived from the result window rather than from `total`.

category.title: Category
category.description: Jurisdictional class. `repealed` and `spent` are accepted for backward compatibility and resolve against `actStatus` instead. Values: `central`, `state`, `regulatory`, `repealed`, `spent`.

state.title: State
state.description: Jurisdiction slug. `central` is a value here, for Union legislation. Live counts per jurisdiction are on GET /acts/coverage.

department.title: Department
department.description: Issuing body. Deliberately NOT an enumerated list: this field holds 943 distinct values and mixes clean regulator slugs (`sebi`, `rbi`, `moefcc`) with free-text state department names (`Law Department`). Read GET /acts/filters for the values with the most data behind them.

actStatus.title: Actstatus
actStatus.description: Filter by the publisher's lifecycle status. Accepts one value or a list. This is the publisher's claim, not our verdict: see GET /acts/{actId}/status. Values: `in_force`, `repealed`, `superseded`, `spent`.

excludeRepealed.title: Excluderepealed
excludeRepealed.description: Drop provisions whose act the publisher records as repealed or spent. Off by default, because repealed law is still law that was in force and is routinely the thing being researched.

isSubordinate.title: Issubordinate
isSubordinate.description: True for subordinate instruments only (rules, notifications, circulars, orders); false for principal acts only. Omit for both.

provisionType.title: Provisiontype
provisionType.description: Filter by what the provision DOES. Accepts one value or a list. Values: `mandatory`, `general`, `prohibitory`, `overriding`, `discretionary`, `declaratory`.

sectionType.title: Sectiontype
sectionType.description: Filter by structural kind of the passage. Accepts one value or a list. Values: `amendment_provision`, `article`, `body`, `chapter_heading`, `definition_clause`, `definitions`, `part_heading`, `preamble`, `schedule`, `section`, `short_title`, `sub_section`.

legalSubject.title: Legalsubject
legalSubject.description: Filter by subject area, classified at ingest. Accepts one value or a list. Values: `administrative_law`, `banking_finance`, `civil_procedure`, `constitutional_law`, `corporate_law`, `criminal_law`, `environmental_law`, `family_law`, `general`, `information_technology`, `intellectual_property`, `labour_law`, `property_law`, `tax_law`.

matchType.title: Matchtype
matchType.description:
How query terms must appear in the provision text. `any` (the default) leaves hybrid ranking to do the work; `all` keeps only provisions containing EVERY query term; `phrase` keeps only those containing the exact phrase.

⚠️ It narrows the ranked candidate pool rather than re-querying the index, so a `phrase` search returns phrase matches WITHIN the top candidates, not every phrase match in the corpus. For an exhaustive phrase search, narrow with the structured filters first.

Values: `any`, `all`, `phrase`.

page.title: Page
page.description: 1-based page number. `page * pageSize` may not exceed 100; narrow the query with filters to reach deeper matches.

yearFrom.title: Yearfrom
yearFrom.description: Earliest year of enactment to include, inclusive. Matched against the publisher's own year field, which is occasionally corrupt, so there is no lower bound and a value below 1800 is a legitimate way to find those rows.

yearTo.title: Yearto
yearTo.description: Latest year of enactment to include, inclusive.

sectionNumber.title: Sectionnumber
sectionNumber.description: Filter by exact section number. The publisher's own numbering, which is not an integer: `498A`, `376DA` and `2-A` all occur, and the alphabetic suffix is part of the number rather than a sub-provision.

actTitle.title: Acttitle
actTitle.description: Filter by words in the act's title. Each word must appear, so `Bharatiya Nyaya` narrows to the Sanhita.

ActSearchRequest.title: ActSearchRequest
ActSearchRequest.description: Search Indian legislation by semantic query.

enactmentDate.title: Enactmentdate
enactmentDate.description: Enactment date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null when the publisher's stored value is not a date we can state without guessing. See `enactmentDateRaw`.

enactmentDateRaw.title: Enactmentdateraw
enactmentDateRaw.description: The publisher's own string, present only when it differs from `enactmentDate`. 21% of the corpus stores `23-Nov-2001`, and a small tail stores values that are not dates at all.

relevanceScore.title: Relevancescore
relevanceScore.description: Ranking score for this result against the query, after hybrid fusion and cross-encoder reranking. Comparable WITHIN one response and not across responses: it is a rank artifact, not a probability, and not a statement about legal relevance.

sourceUrlNote.title: Sourceurlnote
sourceUrlNote.description: Why `sourceUrl` is absent, when it is. A named reason, because a bare null cannot be told apart from 'not applicable'.

citation.description: How to cite this provision. Present on 99.90% of served acts.

ActSearchResult.title: ActSearchResult
ActSearchResult.description: A single legislation search result with full metadata.

subSection.title: Subsection
subSection.description: The sub-provision marker this passage sits under, e.g. `(8)`.

titleRegional.title: Titleregional
titleRegional.description: The instrument's title in its regional language, where the publisher gives one. Held for a small fraction of the corpus.

parent.description: For a subordinate instrument, the act it was made under.

goodLawStatus.title: Goodlawstatus
goodLawStatus.description: Derived currency verdict for the ACT this provision belongs to: `good_law`, `not_good_law` or `unknown`. See GET /acts/{actId}/status for the reason and the underlying claims.

amendmentCount.title: Amendmentcount
amendmentCount.description: The publisher's own amendment count for this provision. ⚠️ It does NOT always agree with what we hold: many acts carry a non-zero count with no parseable amendment record behind it. Read GET /acts/{actId}/sections/{n}/history for the events we actually hold, and its `coverage` block for the difference. The corpus-wide gap is `depth.actsClaimingAmendmentsWithoutEvents` on the free GET /acts/coverage.

amendmentYears.title: Amendmentyears
amendmentYears.description: Distinct years in which this provision was amended.

limitationPeriods.title: Limitationperiods
limitationPeriods.description: Time limits stated in the provision's own text, e.g. `90 days`. Extracted, not adjudicated: read the text before relying on one.

effectiveDates.title: Effectivedates
effectiveDates.description: Dates the provision's text names as taking effect.

wordCount.title: Wordcount
wordCount.description: Summed across every passage of this provision. The stored field is per passage, so one passage's value would understate a long section.

text.title: Text
text.description: The publisher's text for this provision, sliced from the act document by the stored character offsets. Never a concatenation of retrieval passages: those carry a synthesized header that is ours, not the publisher's.

available.title: Available
available.description: Whether the provision's text could be reproduced. False with a `note` when we hold the provision and cannot serve its text; a null `text` alone cannot be told apart from an empty provision. A false answer here is refunded.

note.title: Note
note.description: Why `available` is false, when it is.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: What this text is and is not. It is the publisher's published text; we do NOT apply amendments to it. See GET /acts/{actId}/sections/{n}/history.

resolvedFrom.description: How your act_id or section number was matched, when it did not match exactly as sent. Null when it did.

hasMore.title: Hasmore
hasMore.description: True when more events exist beyond this page.

resolvedFrom.description: How your act_id or section number was matched, when it did not match exactly as sent. Null when it did.
How your act_id or section number was matched, when it did not match exactly as sent. Null when it did.

goodLawStatus.title: Goodlawstatus
goodLawStatus.description: Our DERIVED verdict: `good_law`, `not_good_law` or `unknown`. Conservative by construction -- an unverified repeal claim maps to `unknown`, NEVER to `not_good_law`, because we do not check whether a repealing instrument was brought into force and at least one repeal on this record involves an Act that never commenced. One field to filter on; the three raw fields below remain if you want to judge it yourself.

goodLawReason.title: Goodlawreason
goodLawReason.description: Why the verdict above is what it is. Always present.

publisherStatus.title: Publisherstatus
publisherStatus.description: `act_status` exactly as the publisher records it. Their word, not our verdict.

servedStatus.title: Servedstatus
servedStatus.description: `served` or `retired`. OUR word about whether this API answers for it.

enactmentDate.title: Enactmentdate
enactmentDate.description: The date the act was enacted, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null when the stored value is not a date we can state without guessing. 🔴 This is NOT the year in the act's short title: 'The Biswa Bangla Biswabidyalay Act, 2017' was enacted 2018-01-09, and on a subordinate instrument `year` is often the PARENT act's year. Use `year` for the title year and this field for the date.

enactmentDateRaw.title: Enactmentdateraw
enactmentDateRaw.description: What the publisher stored, present only when it differs from `enactmentDate`. When `enactmentDate` is null this carries the reason it is null, by showing you the value: a bare year ('1963'), an era year ('15-Oct-1349', from an act titled in the Fasli calendar), or a corrupt one ('0032-03-05').

dateOfAssent.title: Dateofassent
dateOfAssent.description: The date of assent as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null when the stored value is not a date. Some records store an act NUMBER here ('15 of 1992'); those return null with the value in `dateOfAssentRaw`.

dateOfAssentRaw.title: Dateofassentraw
dateOfAssentRaw.description: What the publisher stored, when it differs from `dateOfAssent`.

repeals.title: Repeals
repeals.description: Acts this one repeals, as the publisher names them. The inverse of `repealClaim`, and subject to the same caveat: it is their record, and we do not verify commencement.

supersededBy.title: Supersededby
supersededBy.description: A later consolidation that replaced this version, where one is recorded.

subordinateCount.title: Subordinatecount
subordinateCount.description: Subordinate instruments the publisher records under this act.

resolvedFrom.description: How your act_id or section number was matched, when it did not match exactly as sent. Null when it did.

hasHierarchy.title: Hashierarchy
hasHierarchy.description: False when the publisher gives this act no chapter or part divisions, in which case `nodes` is a flat section list. Most served acts carry no hierarchy, so a flat answer is the common case and not an error. `GET /acts/coverage` publishes how many do, as `depth.actsWithStructure`.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: True when the act has more sections than one call returns.

resolvedFrom.description: How your act_id or section number was matched, when it did not match exactly as sent. Null when it did.

total.title: Total
total.description: Distinct subordinate instruments across all pages, not rows on this page (that is `returned`). Counted per instrument, so an instrument stored as many passages counts once.

totalIsExact.title: Totalisexact
totalIsExact.description: False when the corpus scan behind `total` hit its ceiling, which makes `total` a floor. The ceiling sits above the largest parent in the corpus, so this is true today.

hasMore.title: Hasmore
hasMore.description: True when a further page of instruments exists.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: DEPRECATED. True when `hasMore` is true or `totalIsExact` is false. Read those two instead.

resolvedFrom.description: How your act_id or section number was matched, when it did not match exactly as sent. Null when it did.
Null when the act is exactly the `actId` you sent. Otherwise how your input was matched after copy damage (whitespace, quotes, a trailing period) was removed.

isSubordinate.title: Issubordinate
isSubordinate.description: True for subordinate legislation: notifications, rules, circulars, orders. False for principal acts.

issuedDate.title: Issueddate
issuedDate.description: Date the instrument was issued by the publisher, where known.

currencyStatus.title: Currencystatus
currencyStatus.description: How far the currency of this document can be vouched for. `repeal_tracked`: the publisher records a repeal flag for this document, so a repealed instrument is identifiable. `as_issued`: served as issued on `issuedDate`, and it MAY HAVE BEEN SUPERSEDED since. India Code publishes no supersession status for subordinate legislation, and a superseding instrument names its predecessor only in prose, so this API cannot tell you whether a notification is still in force. Treat `as_issued` documents as evidence of what was issued on a date, not as a statement of current law.

effectId.title: Effectid
effectId.description: Stable identifier for this recorded effect, so a change can be cited and diffed rather than only read.

effectiveDate.title: Effectivedate
effectiveDate.description: ISO date the amendment took effect, where the publisher records one.

effectiveDateSource.title: Effectivedatesource
effectiveDateSource.description: `publisher` when a date is recorded, `not_recorded` when it is not. Roughly half of held records carry no date, so an absent date is ordinary and is named rather than nulled. The `coverage` block counts the dated events for THIS provision.

originalText.title: Originaltext
originalText.description: The wording replaced, quoted by the publisher. Present on a minority of records, because most footnotes do not quote it.

appliedStatus.title: Appliedstatus
appliedStatus.description: Whether this amendment is reflected in the text we serve: `applied`, `not_applied` or `unknown`. Today it is `not_applied` on every record, because we serve the publisher's text as published and do not edit it. The field exists so that a consumer never has to infer currency from silence.

credits.title: Credits
credits.description: Credits consumed per call (1 credit = $0.01 USD).

description.title: Description
examples: Hybrid semantic + keyword search across the United States Code (USC), Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), and supported state statutory codes.

ApiCreditCostResponse.title: ApiCreditCostResponse
ApiCreditCostResponse.description: Single endpoint credit cost for the pricing matrix.

dollarPerCredit.title: Dollarpercredit
dollarPerCredit.description: USD cost per 1 credit (0.01 means 1 credit = $0.01).

ApiCreditPricingResponse.title: ApiCreditPricingResponse
ApiCreditPricingResponse.description: Full pricing information for the API credit system. USD only.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Human-readable reason, safe to surface to an end user. Branch on the HTTP status rather than on this string: the wording is not part of the contract and may be reworded, but 401 (bad key), 402 (out of credits), 403 (missing scope), 404 (no such resource) and 429 (rate limited) are stable.

errors.title: Errors
errors.description: Present on 422 only: every field that failed validation.

ApiDetailError.title: ApiDetailError
ApiDetailError.description:
Error envelope the API actually returns.

Every error (400/401/402/403/404/405/422/429/5xx) carries a `detail`
string, e.g. `{"detail": "Insufficient API credits."}`, on every mount of
the API. A 422 adds `errors`, one entry per rejected field. Some 404s add
endpoint-specific diagnosis beside `detail` (the statutes section routes
add `actId`, `reason` and `didYouMean`); treat unknown keys as optional.

loc.title: Loc
loc.description: Where the bad value is: `body`, `query` or `path`, then the parameter name exactly as you send it (camelCase), then list indexes. A bare `["body"]` means the body as a whole was not a JSON object.

msg.title: Msg
msg.description: What is wrong with the value, in plain English.

ApiFieldError.title: ApiFieldError
ApiFieldError.description: One rejected field in a 422 response.

textReflectsEvents.title: Textreflectsevents
textReflectsEvents.description: How many of these events the served text incorporates. Currently always 0.

isBounded.title: Isbounded
isBounded.description: True means we hold no recorded event affecting this date, which is NOT the same as there having been none. Amendment capture is per-publisher and began long after the law did.

AsOfAnswer.title: AsOfAnswer
AsOfAnswer.description:
A dated question answered with a TIMELINE, never with reconstructed text.

We hold amendment EVENTS and no versioned text, so there is no honest way
to render this provision as it stood on a date. Returning current text
under a date parameter would be a wrong answer shaped like a right one.

Citation.title: Citation
Citation.description:
How to cite the thing this response is about.

Built from the publisher's own title, so where that title carries a defect
so does the citation: some titles end in a period, which reads as
`... Act., s. 3`, and some carry no year at all. Those are recorded defects
rather than reasons to withhold the field. `GET /acts/coverage` publishes
how many served acts carry a citation, as `depth.actsWithCitation`.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: The NEW provision's own heading, as printed in the publisher's correspondence table. It is not the repealed section's heading, and where the recodification changed the offence the two differ.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: How much of the old code this mapping covers, where it came from, and how it was checked. `source` names the government publication the table is transcribed from, so a caller can go and read it. 🔴 It is still not a complete concordance: a section absent here is NOT thereby unchanged, and the correspondence is many-to-many in places. Read `numberedSectionsMapped` before treating an absent section as unmapped-because-unchanged.

CoverageCount.title: CoverageCount
CoverageCount.description:
A live facet hit.

`passages` is what a Qdrant facet can actually count. It is NOT an act
count and must not be read as one: a section spans several passages and an
act many sections. Act-level figures live in `totals` and carry their own
measurement date.

categoryLegend.title: Categorylegend
categoryLegend.description: What each `category` value means. The vocabulary alone did not say.

actsClaimingAmendmentsWithoutEvents.title: Actsclaimingamendmentswithoutevents
actsClaimingAmendmentsWithoutEvents.description: Acts whose stored amendment count is non-zero while no parseable amendment record exists. They return an empty event list, and this number is published so that emptiness is legible as a known gap rather than as an assertion that nothing ever changed.

CoverageDepth.title: CoverageDepth
CoverageDepth.description:
The corpus against the four questions worth asking of it.

Text held, structure held, amendments recorded and repeals recorded are
INDEPENDENT columns. A single "we have it" number would hide which of them
is true for a given act.

sections.title: Sections
sections.description: Distinct (act, section) pairs. NOT the passage count: a section spans several passages, so `passages` is the larger number.

passages.title: Passages
passages.description: Live, exact, counted at request time.

measuredOn.title: Measuredon
measuredOn.description: The date the act-level counts in this block were last scanned.

at.title: At
at.description: UTC instant at which the next credits expire.

credits.title: Credits
credits.description: Credits that expire at that instant. They stop being spendable immediately at `at`, not when the nightly sweep records it.

CreditExpiry.title: CreditExpiry
CreditExpiry.description: The soonest expiry, and what dies with it.

perMinute.title: Perminute
perMinute.description: Requests allowed per minute on this key, plan multiplier already applied.

perHour.title: Perhour
perHour.description: Requests allowed per hour on this key.

perDay.title: Perday
perDay.description: Requests allowed per day on this key.

CreditRateLimit.title: CreditRateLimit
CreditRateLimit.description:
Request-rate ceilings in force for the calling key.

A SECOND, independent ceiling alongside credits, and the two are unrelated:
you can hold credits and still be throttled, or sit far under these limits
and be refused for an empty balance.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the credits came from. `bonus` (signup grant), `subscription` (plan allowance, use-it-or-lose-it), `payg` (purchased packs) and `comp` (complimentary) exist today, and this list is not closed: read the values rather than matching on a fixed set.

credits.title: Credits
credits.description: Credits remaining in this source. 1 credit = $0.01.

CreditSourceBreakdown.title: CreditSourceBreakdown
CreditSourceBreakdown.description: Live credits held under one funding source.

sectionNumber.title: Sectionnumber
sectionNumber.description: Where the term is defined, when known.

creditsRemaining.title: Creditsremaining
creditsRemaining.description:
Credits you can actually spend right now. Deliberately the same field name that metered responses return, so one name means one thing across the API.

Derived from your live credit buckets under the same expiry rule the billing path applies, so it never promises credits a call would refuse to spend.

usdRemaining.title: Usdremaining
usdRemaining.description: `creditsRemaining` in USD, at the published conversion rate (1 credit = $0.01). Provided so you do not have to hardcode the rate; `GET /api/v1/api-credits/pricing` is its source of truth.

bySource.title: Bysource
bySource.description: `creditsRemaining` split by funding source, and it always sums to it. Worth reading because the sources do not behave alike: `subscription` credits are use-it-or-lose-it at the period end, while `payg` credits you bought are durable and burn last.

nextExpiry.description: The soonest expiry across your credits, or `null` if none of them expire. Poll this to avoid silently forfeiting an allowance.

plan.title: Plan
plan.description: Active API subscription tier, or `null` on pay-as-you-go. Also determines your rate-limit multiplier. Briefly cached, so a subscription change made seconds ago may not be reflected yet; `creditsRemaining` is always live.

totalPurchased.title: Totalpurchased
totalPurchased.description: Lifetime credits added to this account.

totalConsumed.title: Totalconsumed
totalConsumed.description: Lifetime credits spent by this account.

rateLimit.description:
How fast this key may call, as opposed to how much it may spend. The two ceilings are independent: holding credits does not exempt you from these, and staying under these does not pay for a call.

These are the ceilings themselves, with your plan already applied, so you can size a client BEFORE issuing a request. The `X-RateLimit-*` headers on every response report the same ceilings plus your live headroom, and the two agree.

asOf.title: Asof
asOf.description: When this balance was computed. The value is live, not cached, so this is the instant the buckets were read.

ExternalCreditBalanceResponse.title: ExternalCreditBalanceResponse
ExternalCreditBalanceResponse.description: Spendable credit balance for the calling API key's account.

effectiveDate.title: Effectivedate
effectiveDate.description: Date the amendment took effect, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null when the publisher's footnote does not state one we can read without guessing. See `effectiveDateRaw`.

effectiveDateRaw.title: Effectivedateraw
effectiveDateRaw.description: The date exactly as the footnote gives it, present when it differs from `effectiveDate`. Footnotes carry prose ('1st April 2017') and day-first numerals ('24-10-2019').

input.title: Input
input.description: The act identifier exactly as you sent it.

actId.title: Actid
actId.description: The act_id it matched. Send this next time.

sectionInput.title: Sectioninput
sectionInput.description: The section number exactly as you sent it, on a section route.

sectionNumber.title: Sectionnumber
sectionNumber.description: The section number as the publisher writes it. Send this next time.

via.title: Via
via.description: What was done to your input, in order. `normalized_id`: the act_id carried surrounding whitespace, quotes, backticks, an invisible character, a trailing period or double percent-encoding, which were removed. `normalized_section`: the section number was written differently from the publisher (a `s.` / `Sec.` / `Section` prefix, a hyphen or space before an alphabetic suffix, a lowercase suffix, or a trailing sub-provision), and matched one stored number and only one.

subProvision.title: Subprovision
subProvision.description: The sub-provision your section number carried, e.g. `(1)(a)` for `302(1)(a)`. The WHOLE section is served: sub-provisions are not addressed separately.

IdentifierResolution.title: IdentifierResolution
IdentifierResolution.description:
How the act_id or section number you sent was matched, when not as sent.

Present only when the input did NOT match exactly. Absent (null) means the
response is about exactly the act_id and section number in your request.
Same idea, and the same field name, as `resolvedFrom` on the US surface.

passages.title: Passages
passages.description: Live passage count where a facet reported one.

JurisdictionCoverage.title: JurisdictionCoverage
JurisdictionCoverage.description:
Acts and sections held for one jurisdiction, in the unit a lawyer thinks in.

Passage counts answer "how big is the index"; act and section counts answer
"how much law do you hold". Only the second is a question anyone asks.

processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems
processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.

creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed
creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged. Read this rather than assuming the list price: refunded work bills 0.

name.title: Name
name.description: The parent act's title, as the publisher records it.

actId.title: Actid
actId.description: Resolved parent, when its title matches an act we serve. Null otherwise.

matchBasis.title: Matchbasis
matchBasis.description: How the link was made. `parent_act_name` means an exact title match, so treat an unresolved parent as a spelling miss or a coverage gap rather than as the instrument having no parent.

resolved.title: Resolved
resolved.description: False when the publisher names a parent we do not hold.

ParentAct.title: ParentAct
ParentAct.description:
The act a subordinate instrument was made under, and how to fetch it.

🔴 Resolved by TITLE, not by `parent_act_id`. The stored `parent_act_id`
values are India Code's own opaque ids and none of them is an `act_id` in
this corpus, so the obvious join resolves nothing. The link is made by
matching `parent_act_name` against a served act title, which misses where
the publisher spelled the title differently, and `matchBasis` says so on
every response rather than letting a caller assume a hard link.

pinpoint.title: Pinpoint
pinpoint.description: The provision as one canonical string, e.g. `302(1)(a)`.

ParsedPinpoint.title: ParsedPinpoint
ParsedPinpoint.description: What we read out of the citation, so a caller can see our reading.

sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl
sourceUrl.description: The publisher's own page for this document, when it resolves.

sourceUrlNote.title: Sourceurlnote
sourceUrlNote.description: Why `sourceUrl` is absent, when it is. A named reason, because a bare null cannot be told apart from 'not applicable'.

title.title: Title
title.description: The act's title as the publisher wrote it.

actId.title: Actid
actId.description: Resolved id, when the title names an act we serve.

resolved.title: Resolved
resolved.description: False when the publisher names an act we do not hold. A coverage fact, not a parse failure.

commencementVerified.title: Commencementverified
commencementVerified.description: Whether we checked that the repealing instrument was brought into force. Always false: we do not verify this, and at least one repeal on record involves an Act that never commenced.

RepealClaim.title: RepealClaim
RepealClaim.description:
The publisher's claim about repeal, with our caveat attached.

Never flattened into a verdict. India Code lists the Industrial Disputes
Act, 1947 as repealed by Act 37 of 2020, the Industrial Relations Code,
which has never been brought into force. Serving that as flatly "repealed"
would be wrong.

citations.title: Citations
citations.description: Citation strings, as a lawyer would type them.
examples: Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act

state.title: State
state.description: Narrow to one jurisdiction. Required for a State-universal title.

asAtDate.title: Asatdate
asAtDate.description: The date the conduct or document belongs to, as YYYY-MM-DD. This is how a caller says which side of the 2023 recodification they mean: without it, a criminal section number resolves to BOTH the old code and its replacement, because both are live law.

ResolveBatchRequest.title: ResolveBatchRequest
ResolveBatchRequest.description: Up to 50 citations, priced per citation.

note.title: Note
note.description: Why this candidate is in the list, when that needs saying.

status.title: Status
status.description: `resolved` (exactly one provision), `ambiguous` (several, all returned), `not_found` (parsed cleanly, matched nothing), or `malformed` (could not be parsed, and NOT charged).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the status is what it is. Always present unless resolved.

duplicatesCollapsed.title: Duplicatescollapsed
duplicatesCollapsed.description: Near-identical copies of an act folded into one candidate. The corpus holds several copies of some enactments, which is a known ingest defect: published rather than hidden, so a single candidate does not conceal that three other records sat behind it.

SectionShape.title: SectionShape
SectionShape.description: Structural features found in the provision's own text.

ApiKeyAuth.description: API key issued from the developer dashboard. Pass as `Authorization: Bearer vq_key_...` (preferred).

ApiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyHeader.description: The same API key as a bare header value: `X-API-Key: vq_key_...`. Equivalent to the Bearer form.

ApiKeyQuery.name: api_key
ApiKeyQuery.description: The same API key as a query parameter: `?api_key=vq_key_...`. Use only where you cannot set a header. A URL can end up in proxy and server logs, browser history and shared links, so prefer either header form, and rotate a key that has leaked.
